# Meet the specialists

Mini-Me is not one assistant but a **team**. The **Coordinator** reads your question and hands
each part of the work to the right specialist. Each specialist has its own colour, so you can
see at a glance who did what.

You don't have to remember this list — just ask your question. It is here so you know what
the team can do.

| Specialist | What it does for you | Ask it things like… |
|---|---|---|
| **Research Planner** | Writes a short, step-by-step plan for your research. It only plans; it doesn't do the work, so you can review it first. | *Make a plan to study the effect of altitude on yield.* |
| **Academic Researcher** | Searches scientific papers and summarises what they say, with references and links. | *What does the literature say about…?* |
| **Dataverse Explorer** | Searches the CIP Dataverse for datasets and tells you which ones fit. | *Find datasets about potato trials in Kenya.* |
| **PDF Librarian** | Reads the PDFs you give it and builds a small library you can search by meaning. | *Which of my PDFs talk about soil moisture?* |
| **Data Cleaning** | Checks your data file for problems (missing values, typos, odd names) and makes a clean copy. Your original stays as it was. | *Clean this file and tell me what you fixed.* |
| **Exploratory Data Analysis** | Describes your data: summaries, missing values, unusual values, and charts. | *Show me what is in this data, with charts.* |
| **Diagnostic Analytics** | Looks into *why* something happened, using comparisons and statistics. | *Why did yield drop in 2022?* |
| **Predictive Analytics** | Builds and compares models that predict an outcome, and tells you how reliable they are. | *Predict yield from rainfall and temperature.* |
| **Data Voyager** | Tests one specific question against your data and returns findings and charts. | *Is there a link between planting date and yield in this file?* |
| **Hypothesis Generator** | Suggests new ideas and explanations, based on the literature. | *Suggest hypotheses about why this variety resists frost.* |
| **AutoDiscovery** | Explores a dataset on its own, coming up with and testing many ideas. It **asks for your approval** first because it uses credits. | *Explore this dataset and find surprising results.* |
| **Report Writer** | Puts everything together into a complete report with methods, findings, limitations and references. | *Write a report of what we found.* |

![Each specialist has its own colour](images/specialists-colours.png)

::: {.callout-note}
Some specialists (Academic Researcher, PDF Librarian, Data Voyager, Hypothesis Generator and
AutoDiscovery) use the **Asta** service, so you need to have signed in to Asta during
setup. The Dataverse Explorer needs **no sign-in**: it searches the public CIP Dataverse
directly.
:::

## Where the data comes from {#data-sources}

When a specialist looks something up, it uses one of these services. Knowing which one an answer
relied on helps you judge it — a dataset's catalogue page and a paper's abstract are different
kinds of evidence.

| Service | What it is | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **Asta** | Academic literature search from the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2). | Finding and summarising papers, following citations. |
| **CIP Dataverse** | The International Potato Center's catalogue of research datasets, each with a permanent DOI and full description. | Finding datasets. |
| **AGROVOC** | FAO's multilingual vocabulary of agricultural terms. | Making crop, soil and pest names consistent. |
| **Crop Ontology** | Standard names for crop traits, varieties and measurements. | Making results comparable across studies. |

If your work uses literature search results, cite AstaBench — the reference is in
**Settings → About**, under **CITING THIS WORK**.
